propositions: Jira rebar-id label is written before local CREATE event and binding are durably published, creating an ordering window where rejected final push on ephemeral runners loses local state while the label persists.

When local state is lost but the label remains, all automated healing paths stand down (binding_walk L10 guard, differ bug-4354 suppression, BindingRecovery.recover_pending_bindings), leaving a permanently stuck unbound_jira drift recoverable only by manual repair.

The L10 guard in binding_walk.py phase-1b should conditionally stand down: replay adopt only when the rebar-id marker equals the deterministic inbound local id AND no binding-store entry exists AND no local ticket exists, otherwise keep existing stand-down behavior.

Replayed adopt must route through existing _apply_inbound_create leaf unchanged, ensuring idempotent recovery via deterministic inbound local id (_jira_key_to_local_id) converges on same local id, binding, and Jira label without re-introducing double-bind risk.

Keys with foreign/ghost markers, multiple markers, live binding-store entries, or existing local tickets must retain unconditional stand-down; only the marked-but-unstored lost-adopt residue class triggers replay.
bridge_fsck unbound_jira audit remains untouched and continues alerting until binding actually exists, as it never consults the label and post-heal the key becomes bound.
